description: Profile current memory usage and identify bottlenecks
steps: Document current memory consumption per dimension loader (dim_market, dim_outcome, dim_wallet, dim_event, dim_category)
Identify the three memory-intensive patterns: full table scan, to_pylist() conversion, in-memory deduplication
Measure Silver table sizes (row counts) to establish baseline: markets ~426K, outcomes ~853K, trades ~millions
Define target memory budget: dimension loading should work within 4GB Fargate task

description: Refactor to stream data in batches instead of loading all at once
steps: Replace table.scan().to_arrow() with record batch iterator using table.scan().to_arrow_batch_reader()
Process batches of 10K-50K rows at a time instead of entire table
Accumulate only aggregation state (dedup keys, counts) in memory, not full records
Implement batch-wise ClickHouse inserts using clickhouse_connect batch insert API

description: Only load columns needed for each dimension table
steps: Add selected_fields= parameter to all _iter_silver_*_batches functions to project only needed columns
dim_market: select only platform_market_id, question, description, market_slug, status, event_id, tokens, updated_at
dim_outcome: select only platform_market_id, tokens, outcome (skip description, etc.)
dim_wallet: select only maker, taker, event_ts from trades (skip price, amount, etc.)
dim_event: select only platform_event_id, title, description, slug, status, category, image_url, tags, updated_at

description: Push deduplication logic to ClickHouse instead of Python
steps: Remove Python dict-based deduplication from _read_silver_markets() and _read_silver_events()
Insert all records directly to ClickHouse ReplacingMergeTree tables (they handle dedup on read with FINAL)
Add OPTIMIZE TABLE commands after bulk inserts if immediate dedup is needed
Update _silver_to_dim_* functions to pass through records without dedup overhead

description: Use ClickHouse S3 table function for direct loading where applicable
steps: Investigate using ClickHouse s3() table function to read Parquet directly from S3 Gold
For dimension tables that write to S3 Gold first, add optional ch-load-from-s3 path
Implement INSERT INTO dim_table SELECT ... FROM s3('s3://bucket/path/*.parquet') pattern
Keep Python streaming as fallback for cases where S3 direct load is not suitable

description: Support incremental dimension updates instead of full reloads
steps: Add --since parameter to load-dims CLI to only process records updated after a timestamp
Use Iceberg time-travel or partition filtering to read only recent data
For dim_wallet, track last processed trade timestamp and resume from there
Implement upsert semantics leveraging ReplacingMergeTree version ordering

description: Update Gold layer EventBridge schedules with appropriate resource limits
steps: Create gold-daily-run-prod schedule with memory override (start with 8GB, reduce after optimization)
Create gold-ch-load-prod schedule at 00:30 UTC
Add memory/cpu overrides to schedule target configurations
Document expected memory usage per Gold command in CLAUDE.md
Write unit tests for streaming loaders (load_dim_*_streaming functions)
Verify row counts match between old and new implementations via parity tests
Test with production-scale data to confirm 4GB memory budget is sufficient
Add memory usage logging to dimension loaders for observability
Run gold daily-run in ECS and verify successful completion without OOM
